title: Evaluator output record
description: Structured evaluator output (E-DI Contracts v1.8 s5). Structured data, never prose alone; prose may accompany it but may not replace it. Every score carries an observation: a dimension with no observation is discarded, not averaged — it forces needs_owner (s5, C27). A record with ratified=false can never be part of an `accepted` terminal state.

iteration.description: Counted from 0 before the first generation, incremented once per generation. Written to the record at generation time (the worked trace in s3: generation 1 => iteration 1).

observation.description: What the dimension was scored on, produced by the channel named below (s5; Contracts v1.8 s5, C27). Required: an empty value leaves the dimension with no observation, which forces needs_owner rather than a synthesised score.

observation_channel.description: Which channel produced this dimension's observation (s7.2).

ground_truth_access.description: Closed enum (s5). saw_gt invalidates this dimension's observation — the channel had access to the answer it was checking — and the dimension then fails.

observation_ref.description: Where the independent observation lives (path, artifact id, measurement). Optional but strongly preferred: the orchestrator must be able to re-examine it without re-running the loop.

pass_rule.description: Echoed from the job packet, fixed before the run. The evaluator reports it; it does not choose it.

class.description: Violation class, so cheap defects route to automatic regeneration and consequential ones route to a person.

observation.description: The quoted text or observed behaviour that constitutes the violation.

remedy.description: The judge's insight into what would rectify the condition, where it has one — omitted otherwise (Contracts v1.5, proposal 0004). A prescriptive judge anchors the maker on the judge's own solution, so this is not required.

verdict.description: RECOMMENDED verdict only. s4: the evaluator emits scores, violations and a recommended verdict; it does not own the loop. The orchestrator is the sole applier of the pass rule, the cap, and escalation. s5: exactly these four values — implementations must not invent synonyms (no 'minor-revision' alongside 'regenerate').

ground_truth_ref.description: The artifact or invariant this scoring used.

ground_truth_version.description: The version of the ground truth in force for this scoring (s1.6, C19). Echoed from the job packet; never chosen here.

ground_truth_hardness.description: How far this judge may lean on the ground truth (s1.6, C19), echoed from the job packet. Supplied per job, never defaulted.

mandate_ref.description: The mandate in force for the frame this scoring sits inside (s1.7, C20) — named with its revision, so a reader can tell which frame judged this.

evaluator_identity.description: model + version. If generator and evaluator are the same model, s4 requires that fact to be recorded with the job.

channel_blind.description: s5: asserts every observation channel met s7.2.

ratified.description: s5: asserts no must-ask value is proposed/unratified. ratified=false can never be part of an `accepted` terminal state.

unjudged_dimensions.description: Dimensions that could not be judged. s5: a dimension with no observation FAILS, and a job containing one can never reach `accepted` — its exit is a forced `needs_owner`, not `rejected`. Do not synthesise a below-floor score for it: that puts an invented number into min() and misreports why the job stopped.

notes.description: Prose. May accompany the structured record; may not replace it.
